evidence: The frozen workbook quality row 5 says the prompt must never name the judge, rubric, dimensions, weights, test paths or grader sentinels. Manual reading of instruction.md:1-9 and all six public notes found only product and launch requirements. instruction.md:5 refers to /instructions and /assets/seed_data.json; line 9 refers to /app and /instructions/integration.md. integration.md:5-9 names public start/health/database facts, not grading internals. The local grader-vocabulary scan returned 0 matches across seven public Markdown files; the literal-ID scan returned 0 matches for all 94 criteria. An additional broader skill-pattern scan covering those files plus seed_data.json also returned 0 matches. Normalized overlap comparison against all criterion descriptions found no sequence of seven or more tokens; the longest prompt overlap was nine tokens naming public controls (ui.md:7), and the two eight-token overlaps describe ordinary cancellation behavior (behaviour.md:9; security.md:3). These are product vocabulary, not copied scoring machinery. Private examples such as CW gate, QC Restart Primary, cw-qc-network.invalid and forbidden-nested-completion are absent from the public inputs. counterexample: Adversarial thought experiments, not executed app scores: a broken app that only special-cases CW gate titles or forbidden-nested-completion cannot learn those private literals from the brief/notes. A conforming app with different labels and API routes is expressly allowed by policy.md:5 and integration.md:5; no public grader ID or exact test route tells it to mimic grading machinery. No leak-based counterexample was found.
